1_Coordinate_Geometry.ncert_source: Class 11 Ch10 Straight Lines, Ch11 Conic Sections, Ch12 Introduction to 3D Geometry
concepts: Cartesian plane, quadrants, distance and section formula
Centroid and area of a triangle using coordinates
Slope of a line and angle of inclination
Equations of a line: slope-intercept, point-slope, two-point, intercept, normal form
General equation of a line ax+by+c=0 and its interpretation
Angle between two lines, conditions for parallel/perpendicular lines
Distance of a point from a line, distance between parallel lines
Conic sections as intersection of a plane with a double cone
Parabola: standard equations (4 orientations), focus, directrix, latus rectum
Ellipse: standard equation, eccentricity, foci, directrices, latus rectum
Hyperbola: standard equation, eccentricity, foci, directrices, latus rectum
3D: coordinate axes/planes, distance formula, section formula in space
formulas: Section formula (internal) = (mx2+nx1)/(m+n), (my2+ny1)/(m+n); external uses (m-n) in denominator with a minus sign in numerator
Line forms: y=mx+c; y-y1=m(x-x1); intercept x/a+y/b=1; normal form xcosω+ysinω=p
tanθ = |(m1-m2)/(1+m1m2)| for angle between two lines
Parabola y²=4ax: focus(a,0), directrix x=-a, latus rectum=4a (similarly for y²=-4ax, x²=4ay, x²=-4ay)
Ellipse x²/a²+y²/b²=1 (a>b): b²=a²(1-e²), foci(±ae,0), directrices x=±a/e, LR=2b²/a
Hyperbola x²/a²-y²/b²=1: b²=a²(e²-1), foci(±ae,0), directrices x=±a/e, LR=2b²/a
standard_results: Three points collinear ⇔ area of triangle formed = 0
Lines parallel ⇔ m1=m2; perpendicular ⇔ m1·m2=-1
Family of lines through intersection of L1=0, L2=0: L1+λL2=0
Parametric forms: circle (a+rcosθ, a+rsinθ); parabola (at²,2at); ellipse (acosθ,bsinθ); hyperbola (asecθ,btanθ)
Eccentricity ranges: e=1 (parabola), 0<e<1 (ellipse), e>1 (hyperbola)
allowed_methods: Pure coordinate algebra: distance/section formula, slope comparison, substitution into standard forms
Locus method: assume (h,k), apply given geometric condition, eliminate to get equation
common_traps: Mixing up internal vs external division sign in section formula
Forgetting the modulus in the area formula, leading to negative 'area'
Confusing 'a' with 'latus rectum=4a' in parabola problems
Assuming major axis is always along x-axis in ellipse without checking a vs b
Missing ± sign when writing both foci/directrices
Treating parallel and coincident lines as the same case
jee_patterns: Locus of a variable point satisfying a geometric condition
Family of lines/circles passing through fixed intersection point
Combined straight line + circle problems (chords, common tangents)
constraints: Pair of straight lines (ax²+2hxy+by²=0), chord of contact, pole-polar, and director circle are NOT covered in NCERT — frequently appear in JEE but require material beyond NCERT
Tangent/normal equations to parabola, ellipse, hyperbola are not explicitly derived in NCERT Conic Sections chapter, which is largely definitional
3D coordinate geometry (lines, planes, direction cosines) is a separate Class 12 topic, not merged here
difficulty_patterns: 14 hard / 20 medium / 0 easy — heaviest chapter by weightage (#1)
Medium questions: direct application of standard forms (line/circle/conic equations)
Hard questions: locus + family of curves + conic property combinations, often needing results beyond bare NCERT statements
hard_archetypes: Locus of a point with two geometric constraints (distance + angle / section + parallel)
Family of lines L1+λL2 through fixed intersection with circle chord condition
Combined circle + line: chord length, power of a point, common-tangent count
Conic focus-directrix condition fused with line/circle constraint
Optimization of a geometric quantity (max/min distance under constraint)
banned_easy_templates: Direct plug-in of distance formula only
Find centre/radius of a given circle equation only
Simple slope of line joining two points only
hard_techniques: Case splits (parallel vs intersecting; internal vs external)

2_Limit_Continuity_Differentiability.ncert_source: Class 11 Ch13 Limits and Derivatives, Class 12 Ch5 Continuity and Differentiability
concepts: Intuitive definition of limit, left-hand and right-hand limits
Algebra of limits (sum, difference, product, quotient)
Limits of polynomial, rational, and trigonometric functions
Continuity at a point and on an interval
Algebra of continuous functions, continuity of composite functions
Differentiability at a point; relation between continuity and differentiability
Derivatives of inverse trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions
Rolle's Theorem and Lagrange's Mean Value Theorem (statement and geometric meaning)
formulas: lim(x→0) (e^x-1)/x = 1; lim(x→0) ln(1+x)/x = 1; lim(x→0) (a^x-1)/x = ln a
d/dx(x^n)=nx^(n-1), d/dx(sinx)=cosx, d/dx(cosx)=-sinx, d/dx(tanx)=sec²x, d/dx(e^x)=e^x, d/dx(lnx)=1/x, d/dx(a^x)=a^x lna
Product rule: (uv)'=u'v+uv'; Quotient rule: (u/v)'=(u'v-uv')/v²; Chain rule: dy/dx = dy/du · du/dx
Derivatives of inverse trig: d/dx(sin⁻¹x)=1/sqrt(1-x²), d/dx(tan⁻¹x)=1/(1+x²), d/dx(sec⁻¹x)=1/(|x|sqrt(x²-1))
Logarithmic differentiation for y=[f(x)]^g(x): take ln both sides then differentiate
standard_results: f continuous at a ⇔ lim(x→a) f(x) = f(a) (LHL = RHL = f(a))
Differentiability at a point ⇒ continuity there (converse false, e.g. f(x)=|x| at x=0)
Rolle's Theorem: if f continuous on [a,b], differentiable on (a,b), f(a)=f(b), then ∃c∈(a,b) with f'(c)=0
Lagrange's MVT: ∃c∈(a,b) such that f'(c) = [f(b)-f(a)]/(b-a)
allowed_methods: Direct substitution, factorization/cancellation, rationalization for limits
First-principles definition for checking differentiability at a specific point
Chain rule / implicit / logarithmic differentiation for derivatives
common_traps: Using L'Hôpital's Rule (not in NCERT) instead of algebraic/standard-limit methods
Direct substitution into 0/0 form without simplification
Not separately checking LHL and RHL for piecewise/modulus/greatest-integer functions
Assuming continuity automatically implies differentiability
Missing chain-rule inner derivative in composite functions
Domain errors when differentiating log/inverse-trig expressions
jee_patterns: Evaluating limits reducible to standard forms via algebraic manipulation
Continuity/differentiability of piecewise, |x|, or [x] functions; finding unknown constants
Higher-order derivatives of implicit or parametric-style relations
Existence/verification problems using Rolle's Theorem or LMVT
constraints: L'Hôpital's Rule is NOT in NCERT — limits must be evaluated via algebraic/standard-limit techniques only
Formal epsilon-delta definition of limits is not covered; NCERT treatment is intuitive/algebraic
Series expansions (Taylor/Maclaurin) for limit evaluation are not NCERT content
difficulty_patterns: 14 hard / 4 medium / 0 easy — despite modest weightage (#4), this chapter is disproportionately hard-skewed
Medium: direct standard-limit substitution or single differentiation rule application
Hard: multi-point differentiability checks, implicit + logarithmic differentiation combined, MVT-based proof questions
hard_archetypes: 0/0 limit needing multi-identity reduction (not a single sinx/x)
Piecewise continuity + differentiability for unknown constants at two or more points
Implicit differentiation + related rates on a curve
Nested logarithmic/chain differentiation with evaluation under constraint
Rolle/MVT style existence with a parameter
Standard-limit expansion path without L'Hopital (multi-step)
banned_easy_templates: Single chain-rule evaluation f'(a) for a simple composite
Bare assertion-reason on continuity definition only

3_Integral_Calculus.ncert_source: Class 12 Ch7 Integrals, Ch8 Application of Integrals
concepts: Indefinite integration as the inverse process of differentiation
Integration of specific rational/irrational forms (1/(x²±a²), 1/sqrt(a²-x²), etc.)
Integration by partial fractions (linear, repeated linear, irreducible quadratic factors)
Definite integral as a limit of a sum
Area under a curve, area between two curves
formulas: Integration by parts: ∫uv dx = u∫v dx − ∫(u'∫v dx) dx

Definite integral properties: ∫a^b f = −∫b^a f; ∫a^a f=0; ∫a^b f(x)dx=∫a^b f(a+b-x)dx; ∫0^a f(x)dx=∫0^a f(a-x)dx; ∫-a^a f(x)dx=2∫0^a f(x)dx if f even, =0 if f odd; ∫0^2a f(x)dx=2∫0^a f(x)dx if f(2a-x)=f(x), else 0
Area under curve = ∫a^b y dx (or ∫x dy); area between curves = ∫a^b [f(x)-g(x)] dx
standard_results: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus Part I and II linking differentiation and definite integration
King's property ∫0^a f(x)dx = ∫0^a f(a-x)dx frequently collapses complex integrands
Definite integral over symmetric limits splits by even/odd nature of integrand
allowed_methods: Partial fractions strictly for NCERT-listed forms (proper rational functions, linear/repeated-linear/irreducible-quadratic denominators)
Integration by parts with ILATE preference order
Definite-integral property manipulation (king's rule, symmetry, periodicity)
common_traps: Forgetting '+C' in indefinite integrals
Sign errors between ∫sinx and ∫cosx
Wrong choice of u and dv in integration by parts (misapplying ILATE)

Not simplifying via king's property, leading to unnecessarily long direct integration
Forgetting to change limits when substituting variable in a definite integral

Area bounded by two curves requiring intersection points first

constraints: Leibniz rule for differentiation under the integral sign is NOT in NCERT

Hard: multi-step combinations (substitution+parts, or property-based simplification) dominate JEE-level sets; pure direct standard-integral questions are rare

concepts: Matrix definition, order, types (row, column, square, diagonal, scalar, identity, zero, symmetric, skew-symmetric)
Matrix operations: addition, scalar multiplication, multiplication
Transpose of a matrix and its properties
Symmetric/skew-symmetric decomposition of a square matrix
Adjoint of a matrix, inverse via adjoint
Solving systems of linear equations by matrix method and Cramer's rule
Consistency/inconsistency of a system of linear equations
Area of a triangle using determinants
formulas: (AB)_ij = Σ_k A_ik B_kj (multiplication defined only when columns of A = rows of B)
det (2×2) = ad−bc; det (3×3) via cofactor expansion along any row/column
det(A)=det(A'); det(kA)=k^n det(A) for n×n matrix; det(AB)=det(A)det(B)
Swapping two rows/columns changes sign of determinant; det=0 if two rows/columns are identical or proportional
adj(A) = transpose of the cofactor matrix; A⁻¹ = adj(A)/det(A), valid iff det(A)≠0
Area of triangle = 1/2 |det of matrix with rows (x1,y1,1),(x2,y2,1),(x3,y3,1)|
Cramer's rule: x=Dx/D, y=Dy/D, z=Dz/D; matrix method: AX=B ⇒ X=A⁻¹B
standard_results: Every square matrix A = 1/2(A+A') + 1/2(A-A'), a sum of a symmetric and a skew-symmetric matrix
A·adj(A) = adj(A)·A = |A|·I
|adj(A)| = |A|^(n-1) for an n×n matrix
Consistency test: det(A)≠0 ⇒ unique solution; det(A)=0 ⇒ check (adjA)B to determine infinite vs no solution
allowed_methods: Elementary row operations to simplify a determinant before expansion
Matrix inversion strictly via the adjoint method (NCERT does not use row-reduction/Gauss elimination for inverses)
Matrix method or Cramer's rule for solving linear systems
common_traps: Attempting AB when column count of A ≠ row count of B
Assuming AB=BA (matrix multiplication is not commutative in general)
Sign errors in cofactor expansion (+,−,+,… checkerboard pattern)
Treating det(A)=0 as automatically 'no solution' without checking adj(A)B
Confusing minor and cofactor (cofactor = minor × (−1)^(i+j))
Believing det(kA)=k|A| instead of the correct k^n|A|
Forgetting order reversal in (AB)' = B'A'
jee_patterns: Proving matrix identities using listed properties
Simplifying large determinants via row operations before evaluation
constraints: Rank of a matrix and Gauss-Jordan elimination are NOT in NCERT Class 12
Cayley-Hamilton theorem is NOT in NCERT
Eigenvalues/eigenvectors are NOT covered in NCERT

Medium: direct computation of determinant/inverse/matrix product
Hard: property-based proofs, consistency analysis, and combined adjoint/inverse identity problems
hard_archetypes: Determinant properties + identity proof then numeric evaluation

concepts: Order and degree of a differential equation
Formation of a differential equation from a family of curves (by eliminating arbitrary constants)
Linear differential equations of the first order
formulas: Order = highest order derivative present; Degree = power of highest order derivative after removing radicals/fractional powers
Homogeneous DE dy/dx=F(y/x): substitute y=vx ⇒ dy/dx=v+x·dv/dx, then separate variables
Linear DE (in y): dy/dx+Py=Q, Integrating Factor IF=e^∫P dx, solution y·IF=∫Q·IF dx+C
Linear DE (in x): dx/dy+P1x=Q1, IF=e^∫P1 dy, solution x·IF=∫Q1·IF dy+C
standard_results: A family of curves with n arbitrary constants gives rise to a differential equation of order n (differentiate n times, then eliminate constants)
A DE dy/dx=F(x,y) is homogeneous if F(λx,λy)=F(x,y), i.e. numerator/denominator are homogeneous polynomials of the same degree
allowed_methods: Homogeneous substitution y=vx (or x=vy when more convenient)
Linear first-order solution via integrating factor
common_traps: Misjudging order/degree when radicals or fractional powers are present without first rationalizing
Forgetting the constant of integration '+C' in the general solution
Sign errors while computing e^∫P dx for the integrating factor
Forgetting product rule when substituting y=vx (dy/dx = v + x dv/dx, not just v)
Misidentifying whether the equation is linear in y or in x, leading to a harder integral
jee_patterns: Forming the differential equation from a geometric condition (tangent/normal property) then solving it
Two-stage problems: derive the DE first, then apply variable separable/homogeneous/linear method
Particular solution problems using a given initial condition
constraints: Second-order differential equations are NOT in NCERT Class 12
Exact differential equations are NOT in NCERT
Bernoulli's equation is NOT explicitly in NCERT
This chapter is restricted to first-order, first-degree equations solvable by variable separable, homogeneous, or linear methods
difficulty_patterns: 6 hard / 5 medium / 0 easy — lowest weightage of the five (#11)

Fewer total JEE questions from this chapter, but rarely trivial: NCERT's narrow scope means questions typically combine formation-of-DE with a solving technique rather than testing either in isolation
hard_archetypes: Form DE from geometric condition (tangent/normal slope) then solve
Linear first-order with integrating factor + initial condition
Homogeneous DE with y=vx and a non-trivial integral
Modeling DE + particular solution evaluated at a point
Formation of order-n DE then solve by separation/linear method
banned_easy_templates: Pure separable with given answer form and no multi-step geometry
